books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Ulysses S. Grant, Personal Memoirs, Chapter III, 1885

stimulus.source_note: Ulysses S. Grant, Personal Memoirs, Chapter III, published 1885. Public domain.
stimulus.text:
Generally, the officers of the army were indifferent whether the annexation was consummated or not; but not so all of them. For myself, I was bitterly opposed to the measure, and to this day regard the war, which resulted, as one of the most unjust ever waged by a stronger against a weaker nation. It was an instance of a republic following the bad example of European monarchies, in not considering justice in their desire to acquire additional territory.

The Southern rebellion was largely the outgrowth of the Mexican war. Nations, like individuals, are punished for their transgressions. We got our punishment in the most sanguinary and expensive war of modern times.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Grant's judgment of the Mexican War in this passage is best described as which of the following?

options.text: He regarded it as one of the most unjust wars a stronger nation ever waged on a weaker one.
He regarded it as a necessary defense of American soil against invasion.
options.misconception: That was Polk's claim in 1846; Grant calls the war unjust and says the republic followed Europe's bad example.

options.text: He regarded it as a war the army's officers had unanimously demanded.
options.misconception: Grant says most officers were indifferent about annexation; he himself was bitterly opposed.

options.text: He regarded it as a war that Mexico had provoked by refusing to sell California to the United States.
options.misconception: Grant does not blame Mexico's refusal to sell; he blames the American desire for more territory.

rationales.A: Grant's own words: the war was “one of the most unjust ever waged by a stronger against a weaker nation.”
rationales.B: Polk called the war a defense against invasion; Grant, writing forty years later, calls it unjust.
rationales.C: Grant says the officers were mostly indifferent about annexation, and he himself opposed the measure.
rationales.D: Grant blames the American hunger for territory, not Mexico's refusal to sell California.
rationales.general:
1. Read Grant's verdict straight: “most unjust,” waged by a stronger nation against a weaker one.
2. Notice who is speaking. Grant fought in the war as a young officer, so the judgment comes from inside the army.
3. Hear the sting. He says a republic acted like the European monarchies it claimed to differ from.
Remember: a soldier's memoir can condemn the war he fought — Grant's judgment carries weight because he was there.
